feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid evidence of scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative with logical progression at NACo and a strong headline/profile aligned to target roles.  
- Good credibility through concrete scope indicators: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack, and studio buildout.  
- Writing is generally concise and professional, with strong domain vocabulary in digital strategy, governance, advocacy, and CMS modernization.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: e.g., traffic growth, email performance, engagement lifts, cost/time savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix consistency/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; maintain consistent comma usage in lists (“workflows and systems” vs. “workflows, and systems”); consider standardizing date format (“Oct. 2024 – Present” vs. “Sept.”/“Mar.”). No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding your most recent strengths would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Replace broad terms like “expert” with more concrete positioning tied to outcomes or scope.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, CMS and platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective large-scale publishing. Strong background in advocacy and stakeholder communications, translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” is repeated in Topline Skills and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening wording and emphasizing leadership-level strengths will make it more distinct and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” not “communication.”
- Replace generic items with sharper, senior-level terms: “Digital platform modernization,” “Editorial operations & governance,” “Analytics, insights & performance reporting.”
- Consider a more focused version: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web operations & CMS administration • Editorial operations & governance • Analytics, insights & performance reporting • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- If space allows, prioritize the most recent/relevant strengths tied to current roles: platform modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search, and cross-functional leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills categories.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Workflow & systems architecture” also overlap with Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and Recent Projects. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign platform development, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact-focused lines, e.g.:
- “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing resource toolkits.”
- “Improved enterprise communications operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content strategy, and user-facing discovery experience.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaigns launched, workflow time saved, search accuracy gains, or engagement improvements.
- Replace generic phrasing like “support” and “advise” with stronger verbs: led, redesigned, launched, streamlined, implemented.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating project detail already covered in “Recent Projects” (AI search, microsite, anniversary campaign).
- “Governance/usability/best practices” overlaps with header and NACo director role; keep only if tied to a concrete result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened around 3–4 standout outcomes and framed to show progression beyond your earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest outcomes into sharper bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel impact more measurable: add email list size, engagement growth, social growth, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements if available.
- Tighten ops/analytics bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast video studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve executive decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video, newsletters, and editorial coordination overlap with the prior NACo role; emphasize enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance here.
- Avoid repeating generic “led digital communications channels” language already covered elsewhere.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier digital/media role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth before the larger platform/governance work in 2022–2024.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to sharpen scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and publishing consistency.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve efficiency, quality control and cross-team execution.
- If possible, add metrics: email open/click rates, video cadence/views, workflow turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “web, email, social, video oversight” language already used in the Director role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize strategic leadership themes not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, higher-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Editorial governance and content operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector and advocacy communications,” “Audience-centered content strategy.”
- Change “messaging” to “communications” or “strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Keep terminology aligned with recent roles: use “content operations” and “governance” since those recur in 2022–Present experience.
- If space allows, consider “Mission-driven digital strategy” instead of “Enterprise digital strategy” to better match public-sector positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in Core Competencies and the header.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is close to “editorial planning” in prior roles; “content strategy” would feel less repetitive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, higher-value platform leadership and execution themes rather than list every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here: remove jQuery unless it is still central to recent work.
- Consider replacing “WordPress / SharePoint / Power Pages” with “Enterprise CMS platforms” if you want this section to feel more senior and less inventory-like.
- If space allows, use one outcome-oriented phrase: “Drupal modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to better connect with recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve specific platforms/tools for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase verbatim.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section above. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “CMS & Web Platforms” and prioritize most relevant tools first: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add level/scope rather than just names, e.g. “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it reads lighter than the rest of the stack.
- Keep formatting parallel with other Technical + IT items; commas may read cleaner than bullets/dots in ATS parsing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- “Drupal” is already heavily evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overemphasizing it here without adding new context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more implementation-focused and current by emphasizing tools tied to recent delivery work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Front-End & Technical Implementation”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope/context instead of just tools: “Front-end development, API integrations, tag management, edge scripting, and deployment automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use versioning; plain “HTML/CSS” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; keep one section broader and this one more tool-specific
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may overlap with GitHub Actions; avoid repeating automation language in both places

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp
- Consider grouping for clarity: Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add light context instead of only listing tools: “Workflow automation, project tracking and cross-team collaboration tools”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are collaboration tools, not workflow systems; relabeling the category will improve accuracy.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale of your email leadership. It should signal enterprise email/association engagement systems without repeating newsletter achievements already covered in NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise email campaign operations • Member/audience segmentation**
- If accurate, add one capability phrase instead of more tools: **journey orchestration**, **list management**, or **email performance optimization**
- Keep it platform-focused and concise; let the work experience carry audience size and newsletter frequency metrics

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that already appears in Director/Associate Director entries
- Don’t repeat broad “multi-channel communications” language already covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it read as an earlier, execution-focused role that emphasizes team-building contribution, production volume, or workflow improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Make contributions more concrete: add scale if possible for the website refresh, livestreams, or weekly videos (e.g., number of events, cadence, audience, turnaround time).
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with outcomes such as faster publishing, more consistent output, or expanded in-house production capacity.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia production. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped formalize day-to-day publishing workflows while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate this role as launching/producing the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating website leadership claims already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened to emphasize ownership and innovation without overlapping too much with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer outcome-oriented line, e.g. “Produced digital and multimedia content that supported policy communications and member-facing programs.”
- If possible, add scope or results: number of episodes, audiences reached, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/projects delivered.
- Keep this entry brief since later roles show expanded digital leadership; 1–2 lines is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/video language already covered more strongly in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; frame it as the foundation for later communications progression.
